summary: The first standards-track specification of the Session Initiation Protocol, an application-layer signaling protocol for creating, modifying and terminating sessions with one or more participants, such as internet calls. It was replaced by RFC 3261, RFC 3262, RFC 3263, RFC 3264 and RFC 3265.

eli5.summary: SIP is like ringing someone's doorbell. It lets computers start, change and end a call or chat without carrying the voice itself.

questions: how does sip set up a call
how does sip handle lost messages
subtitle: The original standards-track SIP: a text-based way to find a person, agree on media and ring their phone.

tldr.problem: Internet telephone calls and multimedia conferences need a way to find the person being called, check that they are willing and able to talk, agree on media formats, and later change or end the session, without tying that to any one transport or conference tool.
tldr.mechanism: SIP is a text-based request/response protocol modelled on HTTP. A caller sends an INVITE carrying a session description (for example SDP) to a SIP URL. Proxy and redirect servers use a location service to find the callee, and the exchange ends with a response and an ACK. Reliability over UDP comes from SIP's own retransmission rules.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2543 was replaced by RFC 3261, RFC 3262, RFC 3263, RFC 3264 and RFC 3265. It is the original specification, not the current one.

facts.label: Methods
facts.value: INVITE, ACK, OPTIONS, BYE, CANCEL, REGISTER

facts.label: Size guidance
facts.value: UDP datagrams no larger than path MTU, or 1500 bytes if unknown

today: RFC 2543 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 3261, RFC 3262, RFC 3263, RFC 3264 and RFC 3265, so it is the historical first edition of SIP rather than the current specification.

sections.title: What SIP Is For
sections.content:
The Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) is an application-layer control (signaling) protocol for creating, modifying and terminating sessions with one or more participants. The RFC lists Internet multimedia conferences, Internet telephone calls and multimedia distribution as examples. SIP can invite people and also "robots" such as a media storage service, and the initiator does not have to be a member of the session it invites others to.

The RFC names five facets of setting up and ending communication: user location, user capabilities, user availability, call setup ("ringing") and call handling, including transfer and termination. SIP also supports personal mobility, because requests can be proxied or redirected to wherever the user currently is, and users can register their current location.

SIP is one piece of a larger IETF multimedia architecture that includes RSVP, RTP, RTSP, SAP and SDP, but its operation does not depend on any of them. It does not offer conference control such as floor control or voting, does not allocate multicast addresses and does not reserve resources, although it can carry the information needed to do those things. SIP is not an extension of HTTP, even though much of its syntax is borrowed from HTTP/1.1.

The IESG note at the top asks groups that need a "name lookup" protocol to follow new working groups rather than use SIP for that function.
sections.eli5: SIP is the part of a phone call that rings the bell and sets up the chat. It works for one friend or a whole group, but it is not the voice itself.

sections.title: Clients, Servers and Proxies
sections.content:
SIP defines roles rather than boxes. A user agent contains a user agent client (UAC), which starts requests, and a user agent server (UAS), which contacts the user and answers on their behalf. A proxy server acts as both server and client, making requests for other clients and rewriting them if needed. A redirect server maps an address to zero or more new addresses and returns them to the caller, but does not start requests of its own and does not accept calls. A registrar accepts REGISTER requests and is typically co-located with a proxy or redirect server.

A location service gives a proxy or redirect server the possible locations of a callee. How a SIP server asks it is outside the scope of the RFC. A location server may use other protocols such as finger, rwhois or LDAP, and may return several locations because the user is logged in at several hosts.

On receiving a list of locations, a redirect server returns it to the caller as Contact headers. A proxy can try the addresses sequentially or in parallel until one succeeds (a 2xx response) or the callee declines (a 6xx response). A proxy that forks a request creates several copies, and a user agent reached by more than one copy must return the same status as in its first response, since duplicate requests are not an error.

SIP keeps little state. Proxy servers do not have to keep state for a call, although they may keep state for a single transaction.
sections.eli5: Think of a receptionist. One kind passes your message along, another tells you which office to go to yourself, and another keeps a list of where everyone is sitting today.

sections.title: SIP URLs and Finding a Server
sections.content:
People and services are addressed with a SIP URL, which looks like user@host, for example sip:j.doe@big.com. The user part is a user name or a telephone number, and the host part is a domain name or a numeric address. A user=phone parameter marks a telephone number so that it can be told apart from a user name. Passwords in the userinfo part are NOT RECOMMENDED because clear-text credentials in URIs have proven to be a security risk.

URL parameters such as transport, maddr, ttl and method, and a ? section that sets headers, can be included in a SIP URL. They must not be used in the From and To header fields or the Request-URI, where they are ignored. SIP URLs are case-insensitive, and all URL parameters are included when two URLs are compared.

To find a server, a client either sends the request to a locally configured proxy or to the address and port that correspond to the Request-URI. If no port is given it uses port 5060. If no protocol is given it tries UDP first, then TCP. If the host is not an IP address, the client queries DNS for address records and stops if none come back. The RFC also describes an optional procedure using DNS SRV records in Appendix D, and encourages naming SIP servers in the form sip.example.com.
sections.eli5: A SIP address looks like an email address. To call someone, your computer looks up the street address of their building, and if you do not say which door, it knocks on door 5060.

sections.title: Requests and Responses
sections.content:
A SIP message is either a request from a client to a server or a response from a server to a client. Both use the RFC 822 generic message format: a start-line, one or more header fields, an empty line, and an optional message body. SIP is text-based and uses ISO 10646 in UTF-8. Senders must end lines with CRLF, and receivers must also accept a bare CR or LF. Much of the syntax and many header fields are identical to HTTP/1.1, but unlike HTTP, SIP may also run over UDP.

The request line is Method SP Request-URI SP SIP-Version. The version applications must send is SIP/2.0. The response status line has the version, a three-digit Status-Code and a Reason-Phrase. The code is for machines and the phrase is for humans. The first digit gives the class of response. Applications must understand the class of any code, and treat an unrecognized code as the x00 code of its class, for example a 431 as a 400.

Headers worth knowing include Call-ID, which identifies one invitation or all registrations of a client; CSeq, a sequence number plus method that must be strictly increasing within a Call-ID; From and To; Contact; and Via, which records the path of a request so replies can return the same way and loops can be detected. Datagrams, including all headers, SHOULD NOT be larger than the path MTU, or 1500 bytes if the MTU is unknown.
sections.eli5: Every SIP message is like a short letter: a first line saying what you want, some labelled lines such as who it is from, and then maybe an attachment. Replies start with a number, and the first digit tells you if it is good news or bad news.

sections.title: Methods and the Invitation Flow
sections.content:
SIP/2.0 defines six methods. INVITE asks a user or service to join a session and carries a description of it. ACK confirms that the client got a final response to an INVITE. OPTIONS asks a server about its capabilities. BYE releases a call and may be sent by either side. CANCEL cancels a pending request but does not affect a completed one. REGISTER records the address in the To header with a SIP server.

A successful invitation is an INVITE followed by an ACK. The INVITE typically carries a session description, for example in SDP, listing the media the caller is willing to use. The callee answers with a similar description. Provisional (1xx) responses report progress, such as 180 Ringing, and a final response ends the transaction. A proxy that receives the INVITE consults the location service, forwards it, passes the callee's success back, and the caller's ACK follows. A redirect server instead returns the new address in a 3xx response and the caller sends a fresh INVITE with the same Call-ID and a higher CSeq.

A session can be changed by re-sending an INVITE with the same Call-ID and a new body or headers. Its CSeq must be higher than any earlier request. Users register where they can be reached with REGISTER: registrations are additive, the lifetime defaults to one hour when none is given, and a registration is cancelled by an expiry of zero seconds. Because REGISTER can redirect future requests, the RFC says it is particularly important that these requests are authenticated.
sections.eli5: To call, you knock (INVITE), the other side says they are coming (ringing) and then opens the door (200 OK), and you wave back (ACK). To hang up you say bye (BYE).

sections.title: Transport and Reliability
sections.content:
SIP makes minimal assumptions about the lower layers. It can run over UDP (unicast or multicast) or TCP, and provides its own reliability. User agents SHOULD implement both UDP and TCP, and proxy, registrar and redirect servers MUST implement both. UDP gives SIP finer control over timing and retransmission, parallel searches without per-request connection state, and multicast. TCP is said to pass more easily through existing firewalls.

Over UDP, a client SHOULD retransmit BYE, CANCEL, OPTIONS and REGISTER with exponential backoff, starting at T1 and capping at T2. The defaults are 500 ms and 4 s, and retransmissions stop after eleven packets or a definitive response. Clients using TCP do not need to retransmit requests.

INVITE is special because the callee may take tens of seconds to answer, and a lost final response would leave the caller hearing ringback while the callee thinks the call is up. So INVITE retransmissions start at T1 and double each time, up to a total of 7 packets, and a server retransmits its final response the same way until an ACK, BYE or other stop condition arrives, or 7 transmissions have been made. The ACK itself is never acknowledged, which prevents a response-ACK feedback loop. A stateful proxy SHOULD keep state for at least 32 seconds after the first definitive non-200 response.
sections.eli5: If you shout "hello?" and hear nothing, you try again, waiting a bit longer each time, and give up after a few tries. SIP does the same thing when a message might have been lost.

sections.title: Security and Authentication
sections.content:
SIP messages can reveal who is talking to whom and can even carry session encryption keys. The RFC describes three complementary forms of protection: end-to-end encryption of the message body and certain header fields, hop-by-hop encryption to prevent eavesdropping on who is calling whom, and hop-by-hop encryption of Via fields to hide the route a request took. Fields such as To and Via must stay visible to proxies, so they cannot be encrypted end-to-end. All implementations SHOULD support PGP-based encryption and MAY implement other schemes.

For authentication, SIP extends the HTTP WWW-Authenticate and Authorization headers and their Proxy counterparts. It supports PGP-based signatures, and the HTTP basic and digest schemes. The RFC says basic and digest authenticate only, without message integrity, and that basic authentication has severe security limitations. A 401 response challenges a user agent client, while a proxy uses 407, and proxies MUST NOT add the Proxy-Authorization header themselves.

Under known security problems, the RFC describes a denial-of-service attack in which a rogue proxy returns 6xx responses. A proxy is obliged to forward them, and a client that repeats the request will probably reach the same rogue proxy again.
sections.eli5: Because anyone can ring a SIP doorbell, the RFC gives ways to put messages in a locked envelope and to check who is knocking. Some of those checks are weaker than others.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
Section 16 walks through registration, an invitation to a multicast conference, a two-party call, call termination, a forking proxy, redirects, negotiation and an OPTIONS request. In the two-party example, Bell calls Watson. Bell's INVITE offers RTP audio codings 0 (PCMU), 3 (GSM), 4 (G.723) and 5 (DVI4). The server answers 100 Trying, 180 Ringing, two 182 Queued updates and finally 200 OK, with a description in which Watson accepts only PCMU and GSM.

Each party states the data types it is willing to receive. Because both sides now agree on the media, Bell sends an ACK without a new session description. Later, either side can end the call with a BYE carrying a higher CSeq (2 in the example).

The appendices cover a minimal implementation, how SIP uses SDP, the ABNF grammar, SRV DNS records and IANA registries for option tags and warning codes.
sections.eli5: The examples are like a script of a phone call: who says hello, what they agree to talk about, and how they say goodbye.

Via: SIP/2.0/UDP kton.bell-tel.com
From: A. Bell <sip:a.g.bell@bell-tel.com>
To: T. Watson <sip:watson@bell-tel.com>
Call-ID: 3298420296@kton.bell-tel.com
CSeq: 1 INVITE
Subject: Mr. Watson, come here.
Content-Type: application/sdp

v=0
o=bell 53655765 2353687637 IN IP4 128.3.4.5
s=Mr. Watson, come here.
c=IN IP4 kton.bell-tel.com
m=audio 3456 RTP/AVP 0 3 4 5
